title: Short Stuff: Thread Count
summary: Short Stuff episode on thread count in bed sheets. The hosts explain thread count as the number of horizontal plus vertical threads per square inch and say counts above roughly 400 are often achieved by using thinner, less durable threads or by fraud. They cite a Good Housekeeping Institute expert (Lexi Sachs) who recommends a sweet spot of about 300 to 500 for soft, durable sheets. They discuss how inflated counts were marketed in the 2000s, including multi-ply threads being counted separately, and how the International Trade Commission authorized customs checks on sheet shipments from India, Pakistan and China. They also cover sheet fabrics (flannel, jersey, sateen, percale, silk and satin), satin pillowcases for reducing hair tangling, and fake Egyptian cotton. Includes a sponsor break and off-topic banter.

segments.title: Opening banter and thread count history
segments.summary: The hosts introduce the episode and joke about the show's approach. They discuss how thread count became a marketing number in the early 2000s, with higher numbers seen as better.

segments.title: What thread count measures and the 400 limit
segments.summary: Thread count is defined as horizontal plus vertical threads per square inch. The hosts say counts above about 400 are hard to reach without thinner, weaker fibers, which can fray, pill or break.

segments.title: Recommended thread count range
segments.summary: Lexi Sachs of the Good Housekeeping Institute is cited as saying the sweet spot is roughly 300 to 500 threads, since higher counts often mean thinner cotton. The hosts say the best choice depends on personal needs.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: A brief sponsor break interrupts the discussion.

segments.title: Sheet fabrics and personal preference
segments.summary: The hosts compare sheet types including flannel, jersey or T-shirt cotton, sateen, percale, and silk and satin, noting that preference is personal.

segments.title: Satin pillowcases and hair tangling
segments.summary: Josh says cotton can tangle long or curly hair and that satin pillowcases are recommended for children to reduce tangling. The hosts also mention silk pillowcases.

segments.title: Thread count fraud and customs enforcement
segments.summary: The hosts explain that no FTC rule governed thread count, so sellers counted multi-ply threads as separate threads. The International Trade Commission authorized customs checks on sheet shipments from India, Pakistan and China, which found sheets not matching their advertised counts.

segments.title: Fake Egyptian cotton
segments.summary: Egyptian cotton is described as a real long-staple fiber that is softer and more durable. The hosts warn that many brands falsely label products as Egyptian cotton, especially inexpensive ones.

segments.title: Closing banter and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts joke about a sheet delivery app and Sharknado before signing off and directing listeners to the website and email address.
